message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"ef3970b65cecf08385b3afebd8c4d6ad14789f916a10247d6d916a5c19b12c01","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tx-class-c:lineage:67","source_registry_sha256":"73669019241a96617275447ad5e45b56c17a2d4bd395699448d85850cfc5bafb","units":[{"unit_id":"sec07-u01","module_id":"sec07-m01","objective_ids":["sec07-u01"],"title":{"text":"Where you may not park","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"A parked car can still cause a crash, so you secure it and check for traffic before opening your door.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Parking bans keep crosswalks, intersections, hydrants, and crossings clear for the people and vehicles that need them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Ola finds an open spot ten feet from a fire hydrant and plans to wait in the car.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Vehicles may never park or stand within fifteen feet of a hydrant, whether or not someone is inside.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Ola moves on and parks at least fifteen feet from the hydrant.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking you may stand beside a hydrant or in front of a driveway as long as you stay in the car.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"The middle tier of bans covers parking and standing whether the vehicle is occupied or not.","fact_ids":["sec07-R01","sec07-F03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Hydrant fifteen, crosswalk twenty, rails fifty.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A friend wants to park thirty feet from a railroad crossing. Is that allowed?","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Parking is banned within fifty feet of the rails.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]},"rationale":{"text":"Parking alone is banned within fifty feet of rails, a longer setback than the fifteen feet at hydrants or twenty at crosswalks.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F04"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Parking safely and legally","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Secure the car first.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},{"text":"Know where parking is banned.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson opens the section on parking, stopping, and standing. A parked car may seem harmless, but it can still cause a crash if it is left in the wrong place or if a door swings open into traffic. We will start with the steps for securing a car every time you park. Then we will work through the three tiers of bans: places where you may not park, stop, or even stand; places where you may not park or stand; and places where only parking is banned. Along the way, you will learn the setback distances and how to park on a rural highway.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Securing a parked car","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Turn off the motor.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Set the brake; take the key.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Check behind before opening doors.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Parked cars can still cause crashes, so every time you park, follow the same steps. Turn off the motor. Set the parking brake. Take the key with you. Before you swing your door open, check behind you for any traffic coming up beside your car. These habits keep your car from rolling and keep your door from becoming a hazard to others. They take only a few seconds and are worth doing every time, on busy city streets and quiet residential roads alike, whether you will be gone for an hour or for a minute. Make these steps a habit from your first drive.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"No parking, stopping, or standing","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Crosswalks, sidewalks, and intersections.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Bridges, tunnels, and railroad tracks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Beside a parked car in the road.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"The strictest bans apply to parking, stopping, and standing alike. You may never do any of them on the street side of a parked car, on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk, inside an intersection, between a safety zone and the curb or within thirty feet of the ends of a safety zone, beside an excavation where you would block traffic, on a bridge or elevated structure, in a tunnel, on railroad tracks, or anywhere signs ban stopping. These places must stay clear at all times, even for a brief stop to let someone out. Plan another spot before you arrive.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"No parking or standing","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"In front of driveways.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]},{"text":"Near hydrants, crosswalks, and signals.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]},{"text":"Near fire station entrances.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"The middle tier bans parking and standing, whether the vehicle is occupied or not. Do not park or stand in front of a driveway, within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection, within thirty feet before a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal at the roadside, within twenty feet of a fire station driveway on the same side, or within seventy-five feet of it on the opposite side. Also obey any sign that bans parking or standing. Staying in the car does not change any of these rules.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03","sec07-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Parking-only bans and rural roads","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03","sec07-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"No parking within fifty feet of rails.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Rural highways: park off the road.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03","sec07-R01"]},{"text":"Bicycles on passable sidewalks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03","sec07-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"The lightest tier bans parking only. You may not park within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing, or where signs ban parking. On a rural highway, park off the road if you can. If you cannot, leave enough room for other vehicles to pass, and make sure your car can be seen from two hundred feet in both directions. At night, use your parking lights or dim headlamps. Bicycles may be parked on a sidewalk as long as people can still pass. These rules complete the three tiers, from the strictest bans down to parking-only bans.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R03","sec07-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Setback distances","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hydrant: fifteen feet.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F02"]},{"text":"Crosswalk and station door: twenty feet.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F02"]},{"text":"Signals: thirty; rails: fifty.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap built from five similar numbers. The setbacks are easy to swap, so match each to its place. Fifteen feet from a fire hydrant. Twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, and twenty feet from a fire station driveway on the same side. Thirty feet before a roadside stop sign, yield sign, or signal, and thirty feet from the ends of a safety zone. Fifty feet from the nearest rail. Seventy-five feet across from a fire station entrance. When a question gives a distance, think of what object it is measured from, then recall that object's own setback.","fact_ids":["sec07-R02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the rail setback","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R02","sec07-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Thirty feet from the tracks.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R02","sec07-F01"]},{"text":"Allowed or not?","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R02","sec07-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a friend wants to park thirty feet from a railroad crossing. Is that allowed? Work out your answer before reading on. No, it is not. Parking is banned within fifty feet of the nearest rail, so thirty feet is too close. The thirty-foot figure belongs to roadside signals and signs, not to railroad tracks. Remember the other setbacks too: fifteen feet from a hydrant and twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection. Before your friend walks away from the car, the motor should be off, the brake set, and the key taken.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04","sec07-R02","sec07-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Parking bans in brief","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01","sec07-R02","sec07-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Motor off, brake set, key out.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01","sec07-R02","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"Three tiers of bans.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01","sec07-R02","sec07-R03"]},{"text":"Learn each setback distance.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01","sec07-R02","sec07-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us sum up. Every time you park, turn off the motor, set the brake, take the key, and check behind before opening your door. The strictest bans block parking, stopping, and standing in places like crosswalks, intersections, bridges, tunnels, and tracks. The middle bans block parking and standing in front of driveways, within fifteen feet of hydrants, twenty feet of crosswalks, thirty feet before signals, and near fire stations. Parking alone is banned within fifty feet of rails. On rural highways, park off the road or leave passing room with two hundred feet of visibility. Next, disabled parking.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-R01","sec07-R02","sec07-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u02","module_id":"sec07-m02","objective_ids":["sec07-u02"],"title":{"text":"Disabled parking rules","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04","sec07-F06"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Disabled parking spaces, ramps, and lift zones are protected for the people who hold disabled plates or windshield cards.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Fines that climb with each offense discourage drivers from misusing these spaces.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Pat borrows a parent's disabled windshield card to park close to a store while the parent stays home.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A disabled card may be used only while carrying the person it was issued to, and it may never be lent.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"result":{"text":"Pat parks in a regular space, because the card cannot be used without its holder in the car.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a disabled card may be used by any family member as long as it belongs to the household.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"The card is used only while carrying its holder and is never lent to anyone else.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"The card rides with its holder.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver stops at a red light right next to a disabled space. Is that parking or standing?","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Stopping to obey a sign or signal never counts as parking or standing.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05"]},"rationale":{"text":"Obedience stops for signs and signals are never parking, while true disabled-space abuse brings fines that climb with each offense.","fact_ids":["sec07-R04","sec07-F05"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Respecting disabled spaces","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fines for abuse.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Plates, cards, ramps, and lift zones.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers disabled parking. Spaces marked for people with disabilities, along with the ramps and striped lift zones beside them, must be kept available for the people who need them. Texas backs this with fines that climb with every offense. We will look at those fines, explain why stopping to obey a sign never counts as parking, and then cover the rules for disabled license plates and windshield cards, including who may use a card and when. We will also see which nearby areas must stay empty, even when the space itself is open.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Fines that climb","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"First offense: five hundred to seven fifty.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Fifth offense: twelve fifty plus service.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Obeying signs is never parking.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Misusing a disabled parking space is a misdemeanor. A first offense brings a fine of five hundred to seven hundred fifty dollars. The fine climbs with each new offense, and by the fifth offense it reaches one thousand two hundred fifty dollars plus community service. One point keeps the rule fair: stopping to obey a traffic sign or signal never counts as parking or standing. So if you are stopped at a red light or a stop sign next to a disabled space, you are not breaking the parking rule. You are simply following the law at that moment.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Plates, cards, and lift zones","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Use only while carrying the holder.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Never lend or alter a card.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Keep ramps and lift zones clear.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To park in a disabled space, a vehicle needs disabled license plates or a removable windshield card, and the card may be used only while the vehicle is carrying the person it was issued to. The card may not be lent to anyone. Making a fake card or altering a real one is a crime. Do not block the ramps that let people reach the sidewalk. Some cities also ban stopping or standing in disabled spaces. The striped zones beside many disabled spaces are lift zones for wheelchair ramps and lifts, and they must stay empty even when you are only waiting.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Card with or without holder","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Card rides only with its holder.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Never lent, never altered.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},{"text":"Lift zones stay empty.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap built from the card rules. Learners sometimes think a disabled windshield card belongs to the car or to the household, so anyone driving that car may use it. It does not. The card may be used only while the vehicle is carrying the person it was issued to, and it may never be lent. A second trap is about the striped area beside a disabled space. It may look like extra room, but it is a lift zone for ramps and lifts, and it must stay empty. A question may describe a driver waiting there briefly; that is still not allowed.","fact_ids":["sec07-R05","sec07-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the red-light stop","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stopped at a red light.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},{"text":"Next to a disabled space.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver is stopped at a red light, and the car happens to be next to a disabled parking space. Is that parking or standing in the space? Work out your answer before reading on. No, it is not. Stopping to obey a traffic sign or signal never counts as parking or standing. Real misuse of a disabled space is different, and it brings a fine of five hundred to seven hundred fifty dollars for a first offense, climbing to one thousand two hundred fifty dollars plus community service by the fifth. Keep each case in its own box.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Disabled parking in brief","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04","sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fines climb with each offense.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04","sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Card used only with its holder.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04","sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},{"text":"Ramps and lift zones stay clear.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04","sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, misusing a disabled space is a misdemeanor with a fine of five hundred to seven hundred fifty dollars for a first offense, climbing to one thousand two hundred fifty dollars plus community service by the fifth. Stopping to obey a sign or signal never counts as parking or standing. Disabled spaces need disabled plates or a removable windshield card, and the card is used only while carrying its holder and is never lent. Fake or altered cards are crimes, ramps must stay unblocked, some cities ban stopping there, and striped lift zones stay empty. Next, unattended cars and parking moves.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-R04","sec07-F06","sec07-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u03","module_id":"sec07-m03","objective_ids":["sec07-u03"],"title":{"text":"Unattended cars and parking moves","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06","sec07-F08"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The law sets clear steps for leaving a car unattended so that it stays secure while you are away.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},{"text":"A step-by-step method makes parallel parking predictable and keeps you a safe distance from the curb.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Nico finds a parallel parking space on a two-way street.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"He stops even with the car ahead about two feet out, backs in, and must end with his right wheels within eighteen inches of the curb.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},"result":{"text":"Nico finishes about six inches from the curb, straightens his wheels, and centers the car in the space.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-R08"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking eighteen inches from the curb is the target distance for a parallel park.","fact_ids":["sec07-R08","sec07-F09"]},"correction":{"text":"You aim for about six inches from the curb; eighteen inches is only the outer limit you must never exceed.","fact_ids":["sec07-R08","sec07-F09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Two feet out, six inches in.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-R08"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A driver warms up the car with a remote starter and walks back inside. Does the key rule apply yet?","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06"]},"answer":{"text":"Not yet; the key rules apply once a key is brought along to drive.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},"rationale":{"text":"Remote-started cars skip the key rules until a key rides along to drive, but the other unattended-car rules still apply.","fact_ids":["sec07-R06","sec07-F07"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Leaving and parking your car","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Steps for an unattended car.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F10"]},{"text":"Parallel and hill parking.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"This final lesson in the section covers what to do when you leave a car, and how to park it well. First, the steps the law requires before you walk away from a car, including a special note for remote starters. Then the parallel parking method, step by step, with the distances that matter: how far out to start, how close to the curb to finish, and the outer limit you must never pass. We will finish with hill parking, leaving a parking space safely, and one rule about driving downhill that applies every time you head down a slope.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Leaving a car unattended","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Engine off; ignition locked.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06"]},{"text":"Key removed; brake set.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06"]},{"text":"Wheels to the curb on a grade.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"It is against the law to leave a car unattended with the engine running unless you follow these steps. Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake. If the car is on a grade, turn the wheels to the curb. Cars started with a remote starter are a special case. They may skip the key rules while warming up, but once someone gets in to drive, a key must be in the car. The rest of the steps, like a set brake and curbed wheels on a grade, still apply while you are away. Follow each step every time you walk away.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07","sec07-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Starting a parallel park","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Choose a space with room.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R07"]},{"text":"Signal early; stop two feet out.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R07"]},{"text":"Wheels hard right; back slowly.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"To parallel park, first find a space with enough room for your car. Signal early so drivers behind you know you are stopping. Pull up even with the car in front of the space, about two feet away from it, and stop. Turn your wheels sharply to the right and back slowly toward the curb, watching for oncoming traffic as the front of your car swings out. On a two-way street, you must park with your right wheels within eighteen inches of the curb. Take your time with each step, because a slow, steady back keeps you in control.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Finishing the parallel park","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Seat even with bumper: turn left.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Back to about six inches.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Straighten and center in the space.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"When your front seat is even with the rear bumper of the car ahead, turn your steering wheel all the way to the left. Back slowly toward the car behind you without touching it. You should end up about six inches from the curb, and never more than eighteen inches from the curb or the edge of the road. Then straighten your front wheels and pull forward into the final position, centered in the space. With practice, these steps become one smooth motion, but in the beginning it helps to take them one at a time, slowly and in order.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09","sec07-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Hills, leaving, and coasting","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Angle wheels to the curb on hills.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Check mirrors; watch for children.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},{"text":"Never coast downhill in neutral.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"When you park on a hill, angle your wheels to the curb as the handbook diagram shows, or turn them to the right where there is no curb. When you leave a parking space, check all of your mirrors and look back for anything in your path, especially children, who often play between parked cars. Signal to let other drivers know you are leaving the space. In residential areas, watch for children at all times. Finally, coasting downhill with the car in neutral is illegal, so always stay in gear when you go down a slope. Keep the car in gear on every slope.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10","sec07-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u03-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two feet, six, eighteen","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-R08","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Start: two feet beside the lead car.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-R08","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Finish: about six inches from curb.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-R08","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]},{"text":"Never more than eighteen inches.","fact_ids":["sec07-R07","sec07-R08","sec07-F08","sec07-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap built from the parallel parking distances. Three numbers come up, and each has a different job. Two feet is how far out you stop beside the car in front of the space when you begin. Six inches is about where you should end up from the curb.
